faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a zoologist salary?

This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it. Remember, super is paid on the base rate, not the loaded amount.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the zoologist salary figures?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Zoologist Pay in Australia

When evaluating a **zoologist salary**, it helps to break down the numbers: hourly rate, weekly pay, annual gross, and what you actually take home after tax and super. This guide uses the latest figures from the Fair Work Commission, Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Bureau of Statistics, and Australian Taxation Office. We assume a standard 38-hour week unless stated otherwise.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 for a 38-hour week. This is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most zoologists are covered by an award – often the Health Professionals and Support Services Award or the Professional Employees Award. Award rates are higher than the minimum and vary by classification and experience. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) with exact rates for each award.

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time (May 2026) was $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 annually. This is a useful benchmark for professional salaries, including zoologists, but actual pay depends on your employer and agreement.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual zoologist, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base rate. For example, at the National Minimum Wage, a casual earns $33.05 per hour. This loading is not included in your base rate for superannuation calculations. Super is paid on your ordinary earnings (the base rate), not the loaded amount. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is paid on top of your salary – so your total employment cost is higher than your salary.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Salary

The formula is simple: **annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a zoologist earning $35.00 per hour (a typical award rate), working 38 hours per week, the annual gross is $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. If you are casual, add 25% loading: $35.00 × 1.25 = $43.75 per hour, then $43.75 × 38 × 52 = $86,450 annually. Remember, super is extra: 12% of $69,160 = $8,299 on top.

### Fortnightly Pay

Fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay × 2. For the $35.00 per hour example, weekly pay is $1,330.00, so fortnightly is $2,660.00. This is useful for budgeting and comparing to salary offers.

### Tax Considerations

Tax is calculated on your gross annual salary. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. For a $69,160 salary, tax is about $13,000 plus Medicare. Use our [take-home pay](/blog) tool for a precise estimate. Note that HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included here.

### Using Our Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you type your base hourly rate, and optionally add 25% casual loading with a checkbox. Never type a rate that already includes loading. The tool shows annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with super and tax.

### Summary

A zoologist salary can be understood by understanding your base rate, award coverage, casual loading, and super. Use the Fair Work Commission and ABS data for benchmarks. Always check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides. For any hourly rate, the conversion is straightforward: hourly × 38 × 52. Use our resources for a full breakdown.
